snapshot_note: 2026-11-19: repair round after an outside audit (docs/reconstruction/audit-2026-11-19.md); the statements of this note about EC3 multi-axis design and fys != fy are narrowed by it: EC3 compression with bending and Class 4 sections are refused, and a Rebar material holds one yield in a native file. Earlier: Multi-milestone parity & hardening updates across native SDB codecs (local_axes_matrix, fys != fy, project_info, grids), concrete beam M2 (as_side) & EC3 10-shape V3/multi-axis design, frame tc_limits span axial equilibrium & modal LinearHistory continuation, and OAPI cCableObj / cDatabaseTables facades (405 tests across 44 suites, 64/64 reference checks). Full vendor runtime parity remains unestablished. Merged with the 2026-11-12 additions: plastic Wen links and displacement-controlled nonlinear static (docs/reconstruction/solver-wen.md). Unmodeled source data recorded and refused; modal damping refused on modal history types (docs/reconstruction/unmodeled-source.md). Area mesh/mass/modifier import and native section-code corrections (docs/reconstruction/area-import.md). Automatic frame subdivision modeled and checked against published per-mesh values; span-moment sign, non-prismatic span-load and buckling reference-state defects fixed (docs/reconstruction/frame-auto-mesh.md). Frame insertion points modeled for linear static cases against Example 1-011; frame M2 sign corrected (docs/reconstruction/frame-insertion-point.md). 2026-11-15: first wave of tutorial-video features (docs/reconstruction/tutorial-video-wave1.md): profile LDLT and subspace eigen solver, mass source, ASCE 7-10 automatic seismic load with entered coefficients, Ritz loads and load participation, modal time history, functions from file, Auto Select design and default design combinations, grid/quick-draw/radial geometry commands. Pushover, AISC 360-16 and ASCE 7-16 remain absent. 2026-11-16: second wave of tutorial-video features (docs/reconstruction/tutorial-video-wave2.md): user-defined uncoupled frame hinges in nonlinear static cases checked against CSI Example 1-026, saved states, Accel and Mode loads, pushover curve and hinge-state display, native import of the Example 1-026 hinge records, S2K persistence. Coupled, fiber and automatic hinges remain refused. 2026-11-17: fifth wave of the tutorial-video work, repairs (docs/reconstruction/tutorial-video-wave5.md; the third and fourth waves are in tutorial-video-wave3.md and tutorial-video-wave4.md): frame end offsets, orthotropic and plane-strain areas, combinations as maximum and minimum, design of multi-valued combinations, native import of modal histories, the Ritz projection, video export; the real program was run for the first time, by an agent on a private display. Results of these features differ from earlier versions. Test counts of that wave: 1348 portable tests, 1383 with the local vendor corpus, 107 suites, 106/106 reference checks. Sixth tutorial-video wave (2026-11-18): P-Delta with frame hinges at element ends, the stiffness after a hinged nonlinear case, hinge cases that stop early kept as "not finished", generated hinge properties and the hinge results window; repairs of a hinge at element end I under geometric stiffness, of the geometric stiffness taken from a nonlinear case without P-Delta, and of five findings of an outside review (history frame forces and base reactions, history load kind, combinations with a contributor without results, continuation from a yielded hinge) and, on 2026-11-19, of six findings of its second pass (unit-independent P-Delta iteration with hinges, displacement control through the geometric stiffness, one name for a case and a combination, combinations of time-history cases withheld, native export of history loads by meaning, one rule for history patterns). Test counts of that wave: 1539 portable tests, 1576 with the local vendor corpus, 125 suites, 106/106 reference checks.

status_legend.implemented-tested: Source implementation exists and a relevant repository test or fixture workflow is present; this status does not mean the current test run passed.
status_legend.implemented-partial: Some behavior exists, with documented scope limits, approximations, or incomplete end-to-end evidence.
status_legend.unsupported: Explicitly rejected, absent from dispatch, or represented only as data without a corresponding implementation.
status_legend.unknown: Source evidence is insufficient to claim behavior; needs comparison with SAP2000 v19 or an authoritative manual/example.

Grid lines, custom template, ratio division, break at intersections; refusals.
Closed forms for the divided and broken beams and the area loads.
Pointer drags, clicks and keys through the application.
The video's first building drawn with the mouse against the index commands.

capabilities.limits: Verified through command functions and headless renders with synthetic pointer and key input only; never used by hand. Snapping is to joints and grid intersections; no midpoint, intersection or perpendicular snaps, no back-face views, no cylindrical grids. Areas have at most four joints. Breaking covers joints and frames, not area or solid edges. The frame-window rule, snap radius and previous-selection rule are project choices. No cSapModel facade.

capabilities.feature: Materials from the vendor's CSiMaterialLibrary XML files read at run time (region, type, standard, grade), import of several section-file shapes at once with filters and an Auto Select list, and a file chooser inside the program.

evidence.note: Subset XML reader, unit handling, duplicate rule, conversion to a material and its refusals.
Synthetic files, unit factors, parser errors, opt-in totals and values of the eight vendor files.
Window and command function with tests.
Selection rules, filters, atomic import, tests.
Chooser on std::fs with tests.
Library material to analysis; S2K and native round trip of library names (opt-in).
Chooser to import window to a drawn frame.

capabilities.limits: No library or section file ships with the program. Lightweight concrete, shear reduction factors other than 1, aluminum and cold-formed materials are refused; expected strengths and strains are not kept. The XML reader covers the vendor files and their schema, not general XML. The chooser is not the operating-system dialog. Verified headless only.

capabilities.feature: Shell top-face stresses by the CSI sign convention, shell stress resultants under uniform temperature changes and through-thickness gradients, native import of the gradient load, von Mises and principal values of linear combinations from the combined components, combination results only where every case has them, base reactions including supports created by area meshing, and refusal of unknown response-spectrum directions.

evidence.note: Cantilever strip (F11, M11, top stress, displacements), combinations, missing results, spectrum directions, base reaction of a meshed panel.
Free and restrained plate closed forms; refusals; opt-in CSI Examples 2-013 and 2-014 from the vendor files.
Opt-in CSI Example 2-015: sign of the edge moment and of the top stress.

capabilities.limits: Top stresses, thermal resultants and combination von Mises values differ from versions before 2026-11-16. Temperature loads on three-joint areas, with joint patterns, and on sections without the stiffness they act on (plane and axisymmetric-solid sections included) are refused. The stored top-face von Mises value of a multi-valued combination was combined field by field; since 2026-11-17 it is stored as 0 in both rows of the result, the tables print n/a, and the display refuses it and names the cases behind a combination without shell results. A response-spectrum case stores no area results. Example 2-014 is matched to the independent solution within 4 % on the vendor's coarse mesh and 1 % on its fine mesh, not to the vendor's element.

capabilities.feature: Result forms: shell resultants and stresses (the vendor form's 14 resultants and 9 stresses; top, bottom or visible face, maximum, minimum, absolute maximum) in display units with a banded legend; deformed shape with displacement contours on areas, right-click joint read-out and animation through result steps; plot functions with absolute acceleration, several traces, a horizontal function, time range, extremes and named sets; the vendor's modal participating mass ratio and modal load participation ratio tables.

evidence.note: Shell quantities derived from stored resultants; single-valued rule; refusals. Tests in shell_output/tests.rs include opt-in CSI Example 2-010 (hoop stress, printed and closed form).
Joint results to global axes, area-local components, contour range, legend ticks, vertex-coloured meshes, joint read-out. Tests in contours/tests.rs include opt-in CSI Example 2-010 displacements.
The two forms, value tables, legend, visible-face direction, step animation; headless tests in result_display/tests.rs.
Plot quantities, absolute acceleration, named functions, sets, extremes; closed-form tests (damped single mass).
Ground acceleration trace; absolute acceleration against closed forms and M·a + K·u = 0.
Rows, cells, totals and Ritz target lines of the two vendor tables.
End-to-end through the application: cylinder closed form, strip, the video's tower, the third part's frames, opt-in CSI Examples 2-010 and 1-022 (files under video_results_e2e/).

capabilities.limits: Shell values are element-centre values: no Gauss-point extrapolation, no averaging at joints, one flat colour per area. Derived shell values (principal, von Mises, bottom face, face extremes) are refused for multi-valued results, and quantities a plate, membrane or plane-stress section lacks, and all quantities of plane-strain and axisymmetric-solid sections, are refused; some of these were shown before 2026-11-17. The forces of plane-strain areas are recovered with the plane-strain relation since the fifth wave of 2026-11-17 (before, with the plane-stress relation); their display is still not done. Velocity, reaction, base and energy plot functions are not recorded; absolute acceleration only for modal time histories; plot sets are not saved with the model. Video export exists since the fifth wave of 2026-11-17 (see video-export-and-window-additions); no image export. Display units belong to a form; a units change of the model still needs it unlocked. Windows tested through command functions and headless renders; looked at by an agent on a private display on 2026-11-17 (see gui), not used by a person.

capabilities.feature: Modal participation factors and participating mass ratios in global directions for joints with local axes, rotational ratios (RX, RY, RZ) about the centre of mass, and load participation items for the case's starting loads and the six unit accelerations.

evidence.note: Rigid-body acceleration shapes, factors and ratios (CSI Analysis Reference pp. 339, 376-378).
Rotated joint at five angles, bitwise equality without joint axes, two offset masses, completeness over all modes, load participation identities.

capabilities.limits: RX, RY, RZ ratios differ from versions before 2026-11-17 for every model; UX, UY, UZ ratios and response-spectrum results differ for models with joint local axes. The manual's printed centroid for RZ is read as a misprint (x centroid of the UY load used). Masses that differ by direction on a rotated joint couple the global X and Y masses; the vendor's treatment is unknown. No printed vendor table of rotational ratios was available as a reference.

capabilities.feature: Frames with end offsets and a rigid-zone factor: axial and torsional stiffness on the full length; a full moment or shear release makes its offset rigid in that plane; span loads and self weight over the full length with the part on a rigid arm carried to its joint; non-prismatic sections over the clear length; P x arm geometric stiffness of the rigid arms; output stations from support face to support face, read by design as the ends of the member.

evidence.note: PL/EA and TL/GJ over the full length, released ends (CSI Analysis Reference pp. 130-131); opt-in CSI Examples 6-006 and 6-007 periods within 1 % of the published ones.
Equilibrium and fixed-fixed closed forms for loads on arm and span, every rigid-end factor, with and without releases.
Flexibilities over the clear length, unit-load integrals, free thermal expansion, axial span load.
Buckling of a pinned column with rigid arms against a hand derivation and against the arms as stiff elements.
Station positions, zero moment at a released support face, closed forms.
Members without offsets are bitwise unchanged (fingerprints recorded before the repairs).
Cb and the concrete end minimums with stations between the support faces.

capabilities.limits: Results of members with end offsets differ from versions before 2026-11-17, including P-Delta and buckling of members with rigid arms and the station positions and station moments of CSI Examples 1-010b to d (their published tip deflections are unchanged). Not implemented: the manual's reduction of offsets to a clear length of 1 %, the mass of non-prismatic members and end zones, the geometric stiffness of the flexible part beyond its flexible length, automatic subdivision and hinges on a member with offsets. A partial-fixity spring keeps the rigid-zone factor (project choice). The repairs of loads, non-prismatic members, geometric stiffness and stations followed an independent review and were not reviewed again line by line.

capabilities.feature: Area elements with orthotropic materials (plane stress for shells and plates, reduced compliance for plane strain), plane-strain recovery with stored S33 and anti-plane shear stiffness, a section material angle that turns only the material, one constitutive function for stiffness and recovery, and no drilling stiffness on plane and axisymmetric-solid sections.

evidence.note: Uniform-strain patches by hand, rotated laminate stiffness at 30 degrees, isotropic invariance, symmetry of the recovery law, refusals.
Opt-in CSI Examples 2-015 (orthotropic plate, published and closed-form deflection) and 3-002 (plane beam without incompatible modes).
Two rows of the live verification: plane-strain S33 and the material angle.

capabilities.limits: Area results differ from versions before 2026-11-17 for orthotropic materials, plane-strain sections, sections with a material angle (which before also turned the output axes) and sections with unequal stiffness modifiers. The scaling of the coupling terms by the root of the product of the modifiers is a project choice; whether the vendor does the same is not established. U3 of a plane-strain area has real stiffness and must be supported. A law that is not positive definite, a temperature load with unequal in-plane expansion coefficients, and reversing local 3 with an orthotropic material at an angle are refused. S33 is stored and has no reader (no table, API call or display). The stored von Mises of a plane-strain area ignores S33. Incompatible bending modes of plane sections are not implemented, so plain plane elements are 2 to 3 % soft against CSI Example 3-004, whose files stay refused as imported.

capabilities.feature: Multi-valued combinations (additive with a response-spectrum case, envelope, range, SRSS, absolute, nested) store a maximum and a minimum; the API and the database tables return a Max row and a Min row.

evidence.note: Combination by pairs with unit tests on the worked numbers of the CSI Analysis Reference p. 353.
The same pairs through a response-spectrum solve; stations of a subdivided frame.
Row order and step type in the API and the tables; the multi-valued option.
Eight rows of the live verification.

capabilities.limits: Results of envelope and range combinations differ from versions before 2026-11-17 (an envelope kept the value of larger magnitude, a range was added linearly, no minimum was stored); an additive combination of single-valued cases is bitwise unchanged, and the vendor corpus has only such combinations, so no vendor number tests the pairs. Row order (Max, then Min) and the zero stored for derived fields (von Mises, principal values) are project choices. Only the envelope option of the API's multi-valued setting is implemented. A response-spectrum case stores no area results, so a combination with one has none. API readers other than the result tables (cable force and similar) return the Max row only.

capabilities.feature: Steel and concrete design of a multi-valued combination by states (Max row, Min row, each contributing state of an envelope, each with its own moment diagram and Cb) and by the permutations of the maxima and minima of the interacting forces.

evidence.note: Both senses of a multi-valued contributor: ratios equal to those of static cases.
Permutations of P, M2, M3 against hand-enumerated static force sets; Cb per state by AISC F1-1; Eurocode 3 with shear; concrete column; single-valued combinations bitwise unchanged.

capabilities.limits: Design ratios of multi-valued combinations differ from versions before 2026-11-17 (only the positive sense was designed). The vendor's design manuals ask for sub-combinations of maxima and minima; that one permutation takes the same choice at every station, and that Cb comes from that diagram, are project choices. The permutation of torsion and shears for the closed-section interaction has no test. Concrete beams are designed per state without permutations. Sub-combinations per time step of a history and the corresponding-values option of moving loads are not implemented. The vendor corpus has no multi-valued design combination, so no vendor number tests this. Written after an independent review and not reviewed again line by line.

capabilities.feature: Native import of the modal case and motion type of a time-history case, native export of the modal case of a linear history, and refusal by name of periodic and nonlinear modal (FNA) histories and of Ritz starting loads the solver does not have.

evidence.note: Case-record import; unit test native_modal_history_import_branches.
Round trip of the modal-case index; refusals of the writer.
Ritz starting-load records, S2K eccentricity table, export guard.
Opt-in CSI Example 6-001 against its published values and the closed form; Examples 1-015 and 6-005a refused by name; Example 1-022.

capabilities.limits: CSI Example 6-005a NLMHIST1 ran as direct integration before 2026-11-17 and is now refused (nonlinear modal history is not implemented); Example 1-015 MHIST1 is refused (periodic). The Modal cases of Examples 6-006, 6-007, 6-010, 6-011a and 6-011b are refused as imported for their Ritz starting vectors on link degrees of freedom; with that entry removed explicitly, Examples 6-006 and 6-007 give periods within 0.17 %, 0.02 % and 0.39 % of the published ones, the first not inside the printed rounding and not explained. The modal-case index is taken as 1-based over all case records, which holds in the files scanned and is not documented. Example 6-001 needs its ramp samples attached.

capabilities.feature: Export of an animation as an uncompressed AVI (steps of a history or of saved static states, or cycles of a mode) with the project's own writer and software rasteriser; Object Information with the loads on an object; Grid Only start; I section with unequal flanges; automatic deformed scale and view titles; Max and Min rows and curves; rebar material choice; Messages window; number printing with significant digits.

evidence.note: Frame plan, form and recorder; avi.rs and raster.rs beside it.
Byte layout against a hand-written file, read-back with ffprobe and ffmpeg when present, rasteriser rules, refusals.
Object Information, Grid Only, I-section dialog, automatic scale, titles, table messages, video through the menu.
End-to-end tests (files under video_wave5_e2e/): the video rows of the wave, repairs seen through the windows, opt-in CSI Examples 6-001, 2-015a and 6-010.
Open resets display, lock and planes; with p16_messages_tests.rs, p16_misc_tests.rs, p16_offset_tests.rs and wave5_hand_check_tests.rs the repairs of the hand check.

capabilities.limits: No compressor choice, no cyclic video of a plain deformed shape, no file above 1 GiB; frames match the screen in geometry and colour values, not pixel for pixel. The cycles, frames per cycle and rate of the form, the automatic scale of 10 % of the bounding-box diagonal, the title wording and the printing rule are project choices. Result-table cells keep a fixed number of decimals. The windows were looked at by an agent on a private display (see gui); window resizing and the file chooser behind Browse were not. The window repairs that followed the hand check were not reviewed line by line.

capabilities.feature: Live reference checks and automated tests (106 checks / 1679 tests / 136 suites) and vendor SDB integration regressions covering frames, shells, solids, nonlinear links, catenary cables and frame hinges.

evidence.note: Live runner covers Examples 1-001..1-016, 5-001, 6-003 (including NLSTAT3/NLDHIST2 continuation), 6-005, 7-001, 7-002, and 7-003 (64 checks). CSI Example 1-021 eigenvalues added 2026-11-15 (86 checks). CSI Example 1-026 hinge end states added 2026-11-16 (90 checks). A cantilever shell strip (top-face stress and moment sign) added 2026-11-16 (92 checks). Modal participation of two offset masses (RZ) and of a mass on a rotated joint (UX) added 2026-11-17 (94 checks). Twelve rows added by the fifth wave on 2026-11-17: rigid end zones (2), plane strain and the material angle (2), combination pairs of the manual's p. 353 (8) (106 checks).
Vendor SDB integration regressions for Examples 5-001, 5-002, 5-005, 6-003, 6-004, 6-005, 7-001, 7-002, and 7-003.

capabilities.limits: The live suite is a selected benchmark subset, not the full 336-file vendor verification collection.

vendor_validation_assets.use: Primary local workbook for selected solver verification examples.
Geometry, loads, expected outputs for Example 1-001.
Native v19 model fixture for parser/solver comparison.
SAP2000 v19 analysis manual for solver methods and conventions; not an OAPI method contract.
October 2016 Rev 0 Introductory Tutorial that explicitly introduces SAP2000 Version 19; primary workflow reference for the 13-step GUI acceptance map.
Vendor getting-started manual for UI/model workflow guidance.
Local comparison showing the separately supplied January 2022 SapTutor has a Version 16 introduction; use only as a cross-check, not the v19 workflow baseline.

acceptance_checklist: Freeze a fixture manifest with hashes, SAP2000 v19 provenance, units, expected tables, expected outputs, and explicit tolerances; distinguish vendor references from synthetic hand-built checks.
For each imported SDB/S2K fixture, compare imported object counts and critical assignments to vendor tables; fail or report omitted tables/columns before solving.
Round-trip supported S2K tables and compare normalized tables; test the native SDB reader separately. Do not treat private SDB writer output as native-vendor interchange.

Validate solver cases in order: single frame loads/releases/offsets; multi-axis local/global loads; shell membrane/plate/shell; link linear behavior; modal, buckling, response spectrum, Newmark history; then P-Delta. Unsupported case types and unimplemented loads must return explicit errors.

Add negative fixtures proving solids, unsupported nonlinear link families/combinations, cables/tension-only members, unsupported coordinate-system forms, higher-order areas, and unsupported dynamic cases reject rather than produce plausible results.
Validate constraint definitions separately for every enum type; implement exact Rod, Beam, and Line behavior or reject instead of using generic equal DOFs.

For steel design, validate AISC LRFD/ASD and EC3 hand examples by section family; cover local V2/V3 shear, torsion, axial plus biaxial bending, slender elements, buckling, unbraced lengths, and invalid section/material/code combinations.
For concrete design, validate ACI/EC2 beam and column examples including both shear axes, biaxial bending, reinforcement layout, column slenderness, and status handling against vendor outputs.

Audit the API one method at a time against version-matched CSI OAPI type-library metadata/object browser/API help, with contract tests for names, defaults, return codes, mutation invalidation, units, error propagation, and unsupported methods.
Exercise each GUI workflow end to end: create/open/save, edit model, assign loads, solve, inspect diagrams/results/tables, design, and show clear import/analysis/design errors.
